sections.h2: How did Grandview grow, and what is it like now?
sections.html:
Grandview grew from a farm community into a rail town in 1912 and then into a suburb of 26,000 people on the south side of the Kansas City area, in Jackson County along Interstate 49. A post office has operated under the Grandview name since 1889, and the city incorporated on February 6, 1912.

The name comes from the view off the elevated town site, and the city's own history page tells the local story that early leaders looked at the rolling hills and called it a grand view. Harry Truman grew up working on the family farm here. Many service members lived in Grandview while stationed at Richards-Gebaur Air Force Base, which closed in 1994. Population climbed from 6,027 in 1960 to 17,456 in 1970 and 24,502 in 1980, then held near 25,000 for decades before reaching 26,209 in 2020.

  • The city covers 14.73 square miles of land at an elevation of about 1,050 feet.
  • The ZIP code is 64030, and phone area codes are 816 and 975.
  • The I-49 outer roads were converted to two-way traffic in a $15 million project that finished in November 2022.

sections.h2: What do Grandview's housing numbers say about selling here?
sections.html:
Grandview is a renter-leaning city: fewer than half of its homes are owner-occupied, and that shapes who buys and who sells. Investors and landlords are active, and a tenant in place is a common situation for a house sale.

The 2020 census counted 11,606 housing units in Grandview, and 8.1% stood empty. The median age was 35.2, the lowest of the four Missouri cities on this site, and 23.9% of residents were under 18. About 86.7% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which is a lower share than in Gladstone or Florissant and points to more turnover.

sections.h2: What must a Grandview landlord do before a tenant moves in?
sections.html:
Grandview requires an inspection of rental and non-owner-occupied dwellings before a new tenant can occupy them. The Board of Aldermen approved the ordinance on January 22, 2019, and the inspection happens between tenants, not on a fixed calendar.

The inspection certificate fee is $20 per dwelling and must be paid before the dwelling can be occupied. Dwellings also register every year, with registrations due December 31 for the following calendar year. The fee is $12 per unit for 1 to 50 units, and it steps down per unit for larger portfolios. To schedule an inspection, call (816) 316-4819 or (816) 316-4817. Payment questions go to (816) 316-4823.

This matters for a seller in two ways. If you rent the house out, a buyer who plans to keep it as a rental will ask whether the current registration is paid and the last inspection certificate is on file. If you plan to sell to an owner who will live there, a vacant house between tenants is easier to show and to close.

  • Pull your registration receipt and your latest inspection certificate before you list.
  • Check the city's rental map to see whether the address falls in the registration area.
  • Ask Building Services whether a lapse in registration carries a fee.

sections.h2: How do Jackson County assessments and tax bills affect a Grandview sale?
sections.html:
Jackson County values the house, bills the tax and keeps the deed record, and Grandview residents deal with the county for all three. The Assessment Department values real property from its office at 1300 Washington Street in Kansas City, and its phone number is (816) 881-1330.

Residential property is assessed at 19% of market value. The county's own example runs a $110,000 house through that rate to $20,900 in assessed value, subtracts an exemption to reach a taxable value of $9,500, divides by 100 and multiplies by a levy rate of $7.8368 for a $744.50 bill. The Collections Department says it cannot lower an assessed value, a levy rate or a bill. If you disagree with a value, prepare evidence and ask the Assessment Department about its informal review.

Statements go out in November, and payment is due by December 31. Checks are payable to the Jackson County Collector and can be dropped off at Grandview City Hall as long as the bill is not three or more years past due. Credit and debit cards are accepted. Many bills go to mortgage servicers with escrow accounts, so ask your lender for the amount it paid. Senior residents may qualify for an extended payment plan, and the city's tax page lists (816) 881-3232 for details.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Jackson County?
sections.html:
A deed costs $23 for the first page and $3 for each added page at the Jackson County Recorder of Deeds, for documents received on or after August 28, 2026. The county posted that notice with its new fee table, so any older figure you see is out of date.

Of the $23 first-page fee, $8 goes to the State of Missouri for the Local Preservation Fund, the State Surveyor Fund, the State Housing Trust Fund and the County Recorder's Fund. The other $15 stays with the county. Paying by debit or credit card at the office adds a 2.75% processing fee on the whole transaction, and mailed checks should be made out to the Recorder of Deeds Department.

  • Releases and assignments add $5 for each additional affected number.
  • Certified copies of a document cost $1 per document, plus $2 for the first page and $1 for each added page.
  • Most closings are handled by a title company, which usually submits the deed for you.

sections.h2: Which schools, employers and projects shape Grandview's market?
sections.html:
Most of Grandview belongs to the Grandview C-4 School District, which runs six elementary schools, one middle school, Grandview Senior High School and an alternative school. A small portion falls in Hickman Mills C-1. The Mid-Continent Public Library has a branch in town.

The largest employers in the city's 2016 financial report were the Grandview C-4 district with 584 employees, Peterson Manufacturing with 539, Mead Westvaco Calmar with 340, the city with 206 and Ruskin Company with 196. More recent additions include a National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration office, the first building in Southpointe Business Park in 2015, and an Opportunity Zone investment in the industrial area in 2018. The city also reports a 400-unit expansion of Grand Summit Apartments and renovation of three major retail centers.

Buyers pay attention to those projects because new apartments and retail change nearby traffic and demand. If your house is near I-49 or Main Street, mention the improvements in your listing or in your conversation with a purchaser.

sections.h2: How should a Grandview owner choose between a listing, a landlord sale and a direct purchase?
sections.html:
The choice depends on whether the house is empty, tenant-occupied or in need of work, and on how soon you want to be done.

  • A traditional listing works best on a move-in ready house. It brings showings and the buyer's own inspection.
  • A sale with tenants in place can go to an investor who values the lease. Share the rental registration and the inspection history up front.
  • A direct purchase by a cash buyer can close without repairs, and the buyer takes the house in its current condition.

Whichever way you go, ask for the net figure after taxes, any lien payoff, title charges and recording. A written offer that spells out those items is easier to compare than a headline number.

faqs.q: Does Grandview require an inspection when a house is sold?
faqs.a: The city's building pages describe inspections for new construction and for rentals between tenants. If you sell a rental, the buyer who rents it out will need the registration and a fresh inspection certificate before a new tenant moves in.

faqs.q: How much is the rental inspection certificate in Grandview?
faqs.a: $20 per dwelling. It must be paid before the dwelling can be occupied, and the city will not issue the certificate until payment is made.

faqs.q: Where do I pay real estate tax on a Grandview house?
faqs.a: To the Jackson County Collector, by December 31. The county mails statements in November, and the city accepts payment at City Hall while the bill is under three years past due.

faqs.q: What does it cost to file a deed for a Grandview sale?
faqs.a: $23 for the first page and $3 for each additional page at the Jackson County Recorder of Deeds, for documents received on or after August 28, 2026. Card payments add 2.75%.
